stories.headline: Trump reportedly rejects Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days

sources.body:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says his country has proposed a deal to the US that would see the Strait of Hormuz reopened within a week.

Araghchi told reporters at the UN in New York that this could be done "if the necessary conditions are met" and said these were contained within the memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed in June.

"The choice now rests with the United States," he said, adding the plan was delivered to the US via Qatar.

Asked about the Iranian offer, a US official told the BBC positive discussions were taking place through mediators, including about nuclear issues.

While the US has yet to deliver its official response to the proposal, the Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, reported that US President Donald Trump had rejected the deal.

Trump was privately sceptical that Iran would meet his demands, it reported, and had told his staff that he saw a renewed bombing campaign as likely.

The US and Israel launched air strikes on Iran on 28 February. Iran responded by attacking Israel and US bases in the Gulf and Arab Gulf allies of the US - as well as blocking the Strait of Hormuz.

Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to pass through the strait before the war and its closure has caused wild fluctuations of energy prices.

It has also increased pressure on Trump to find a way of ending the conflict - particularly as the US heads to Congressional elections in November.

"If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, a normal maritime passage restored within seven days," Araghchi told reporters.

He did not specify what steps Iran wanted the US to take but added that "the actions that the United States should take are not new. They are all already in the MOU".

"I can tell you if there is seriousness in the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," he added.

A US official told the BBC that the US was "in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz, so we are not in a rush".

In an interview with CBS News, the BBC's US partner, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that the ceasefire process "will begin from the very day they accept it".

"We had previously reached an agreement based on the MOU that was signed in Pakistan... if the United States agrees to proceed in that way, everything will return to the way it was before," he added.

Pezeshkian also said Iran would now allow UN nuclear inspectors into the country.

Rejecting claims that Iran is trying to develop a nuclear weapon, the Iranian president said: "If they wish to come in and have inspections, we can reach accords and agreements vis-à-vis that specific topic within the negotiations."

The MOU between the US and Iran, signed on 18 June, was designed to bring about a ceasefire and at least partly reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The 14-point agreement said Iran would never have a nuclear weapon. It noted that the US, Iran and their allies would end military operations on "all fronts" and contained provisions including the end of a US naval blockade and sanctions relief.
sources.headline: Iran offers US deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days

sources.body:
Tehran awaits official response to plan, but US president is said to expect renewed strikes after midterms

Iran is ⁠awaiting an official US response to its proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the Middle East war as Donald Trump was reported to have rejected the deal.

Iran raised the diplomatic initiative at the UN general assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted ⁠to the Americans via Qatari mediators and could ⁠reopen the strategic waterway and put an end ​to hostilities in the region within seven days.

But the US president is sceptical and has told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November US midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing unnamed US officials.

Earlier, a US official had ⁠said discussions with Iran through mediators were “positive and constructive”.

Iran has offered to reopen the strait of Hormuz and resume talks on its nuclear programme in seven days if the US lifted its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waived sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observed a ceasefire that would include Lebanon.

The Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, detailed the proposal to reporters outside the UN security council on Friday, saying the country would also restart stalled talks with the US on Iran’s nuclear programme. “The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan,” he said.

Araghchi said the initial steps would take about four to five days to complete, and the strait would be open on the sixth day. “And on day seven, the talks with the US will be started for the final deal on mutually agreed subjects,” he said, referring to the nuclear programme.

“If there is seriousness on the US side to ⁠come to a deal and reopen the strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared,” Araqchi said.

The Iranians also engaged their Saudi rivals regarding the strait, underscoring the stakes of a seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted oil flows through one of the world’s most critical shipping lanes and taken a toll on the global economy.

Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the CBS show Face the Nation, said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear programme and other issues, but would not accept “bullying or coercion”.

“Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that “we’re not supposed to develop nuclear weapons“.

Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed ‌to end the war, which began on 28 February with US and Israeli attacks.

Since then the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran’s conventional forces and damaging its already ailing economy.

Trump has previously said he was in no rush to reach a deal, even as high oil prices fuel inflation. On the Iranian side, there are questions as to whether the hardliners who dominate the security forces would accept compromises championed by moderates such as Pezeshkian.
sources.headline: Trump reportedly rejects Iran’s seven-day peace deal to reopen strait of Hormuz

sources.body: US President Donald Trump has reportedly rejected an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the proposal to Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff a day earlier on the sidelines of a UN gathering in New York. The plan stipulated that the important waterway would reopen seven days after an agreement was reached.
sources.headline: Trump reportedly rejects Iran’s seven-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz

stories.headline: OpenAI says its AI agents posted users’ images online and accessed US government websites

sources.body:
OpenAI has acknowledged that it alerted "dozens" of global institutions that their websites may have been meddled with by its AI bots acting improperly.

AI agents attempted to get information from "governments, universities, public agencies, and other institutions", including the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Census Bureau and Education Department, the company said.

The disclosures come days after Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that OpenAI agents had breached non-public files on the website of its government-run health care scheme.

Since August, public fears have grown over the potentially serious, even life-threatening, impacts of AI tools falling outside of human control.

OpenAI said that some of the data was accessed by AI agents, essentially bots that are designed and trained to operate somewhat autonomously, which were working to find "authoritative sources of public information".

But the company noted that some of the bots went beyond that and worked to bypass security measures on websites.

When attempting to get information from the Census Bureau, for instance, AI agents used tools reserved for software developers to access it, the company said.

OpenAI said all of the government data accessed by bots was public.

However, it noted that information that its bots accessed from the SEC, which regulates the US stock market and protects investors, was later published by AI agents on another website. OpenAI says this action was not intended.

In other instances that OpenAI disclosed on Friday, its AI agents transferred data when it should not have.

Such activity resulted in at least 53 incidents where an OpenAI agent took an image from ChatGPT user activity and transferred it elsewhere.

The company said that in each instance of a user image being used and transferred by an AI agent, the user had opted in to allow OpenAI to train models using their data.

Nevertheless, OpenAI admitted: "This is not an appropriate use of this data."

It added that the leak of user images occurred before it had put in place new safeguards on AI training, and it was working to get all the user images transferred to any third-party removed.

Reuters first reported the expanded investigations. OpenAI also published details to its public blog.

In certain instances of the agent activity, OpenAI said the tools "bypassed" security controls of some websites.

In other instances, the AI agents showed "misalignment" in attempts to get at information from websites. Misalignment is a term used by AI companies and researchers to describe instances where an AI tool did something that it was not trained to do or was otherwise unintended.

OpenAI said that it was limiting identifying what entities were impacted because many had asked the company to not disclose details.

"Our goal is to give each organization the facts and defer to them on if and when to make the incident public," it said.

Not all of the instances involved in this incident were being considered a significant security breach, the company noted.
sources.headline: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sources.body: ChatGPT's AI agents have sidestepped OpenAI policy and posted some users’ images online without permission, the company said on Friday. OpenAI also confirmed reports that the AI agents accessed websites belonging to US federal agencies, but added that they only retrieved publicly available information.
sources.headline: ChatGPT says its rogue AI agents posted users’ images online, entered federal website

sources.body:
As the UN warns traditional safeguards are ‘unravelling’, Donald Trump says he will encourage, not restrain, the AI race

W hen the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese , sat down for an interview in the heart of Silicon Valley at the weekend he had known for two days that his was the first government known to have been attacked by a rogue AI agent.

He didn’t reveal the attack then, but he sounded a warning about the march of AI: “the risk is that AI develops in a way in which humans are no longer in control of what AI is producing.”

But Albanese noted, too, that two countries – the US and China – would dominate the world’s response to the new technology.

“The truth is they’re the big two giants here, and so we want to see cooperation,” Albanese said.

“The US is essentially ahead of China when it comes to the race that is on for the development of this new technology. But it is in the world’s interests that there be engagement.”

Days later, Albanese used the global attention of the United Nations general assembly meeting in New York to reveal that Australia’s government healthcare system, Medicare, had been attacked by an OpenAI agent in June, but that it was three months before his government was told.

Again he warned of “the potential risks of allowing frontier AI to develop too fast without guardrails ”.

China’s president, Xi Jinping , skipped the general assembly in favour of a bilateral meeting with the US president, where he emphasised the responsibility to manage AI “for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the wellbeing of the people”.

But the president of the United States – the nation which is the global leader in artificial intelligence – used his general assembly address to insist he would only encourage, not restrain, the AI race .

To little fanfare earlier in the week, the UN’s independent international scientific panel on AI warned a threshold had already been crossed.

There was, the panel, said: “ no assurance that humans can reliably keep AI agents under control today, particularly as they become more capable, harder to monitor and better at finding loopholes or hiding their activity”.

The Australian government had known the reality of this for more than a week. OpenAI had known it more than a month.

Two days after the panel’s statement, the Australian prime minister belatedly revealed an OpenAI agent had hacked medical data held by Australia’s universal health care provider, Medicare.

No patient data had been accessed, but the agent had gained unauthorised access to “non-public files”.

OpenAI’s agent hacked the government sites in June of this year. OpenAI discovered its agent had gone rogue in August. It did not tell the Australian government until 10 September, and then only with a solitary email to a generic public email address not checked until the next day. The prime minister was informed on 18 September.

It was another week before the Australian people were told.

Australia has promised, if it is possible, to lay criminal charges, though this is complicated by the fact that OpenAI claims the hack was committed by an AI agent – apparently acting beyond its instructions (euphemised by OpenAI as “misaligned behaviour”) – not a person.
sources.headline: OpenAI hack on Australian government reveals anxiety at heart of global artificial intelligence dilemma

stories.headline: Fighting intensifies in Ethiopia as rebel alliance expands against the federal government

sources.body:
Fighting has erupted in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray between regional forces and the national army.

Tigray residents, who have been trying to recover from a brutal two-year war that ended in 2022, fear a return to full-scale conflict.

There are reports of panic buying - and now internet and call services have been disrupted.

This means people cannot get access to their money via digital apps in what has become a largely cashless society after ATMs stopped working several months ago.

It follows more than six months of worsening relations between the government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that runs Tigray.

The African Union (AU) brokered a peace deal, known as the Pretoria Agreement, between the two sides, ending the war nearly four years ago - but several issues have remained unresolved that have inflamed tensions.

This year, both sides have been trading blame while troops have mobilised amid pockets of fighting.

This week, major clashes erupted in Tigray and quickly spread into the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions. The two sides disagree over who started the latest escalation.

The TPLF says it was responding to a federal offensive, including drone strikes, while the government says Tigrayan forces attacked first after seizing control of airports in Tigray.

For much of Tigray's modern political history, it has been governed by the TPLF, which first emerged as an armed movement in the 1970s fighting Ethiopia's military government.

It became a major force in the overthrow of the Marxist regime in 1991 and went on to become the most powerful component of the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), the coalition that governed the ethnically diverse country for nearly three decades.

At times this proved contentious as some felt the TPLF held too much sway as Tigrayans only make up around 6% of Ethiopia's population.

When Abiy Ahmed became prime minister in 2018, he replaced the EPRDF with the Prosperity Party, significantly watering down the TPLF's influence.

Relations between Addis Ababa and the TPLF rapidly deteriorated until war erupted in 2020 in what was one of the most deadly conflicts this century.

The AU mediator estimated some 600,000 people died during the war, which totally cut off Tigray from the outside world and drove the region to the precipice of famine.

An uneasy truce was agreed in November 2022.

There are four key issues - and two concern the fertile area of western Tigray.

The TPLF lost control of this territory in the early days of the war to Amhara, a region which neighbours Tigray to the west and whose fighters had fought on the side of the Ethiopian army.

Many people in Amhara believe the territory of western Tigray should never have been incorporated into Tigray when regional boundaries were redrawn after the military regime was ousted in 1991.

When its fighters seized control during the recent civil war, hundreds of thousands of ethnic Tigrayan people fled and are now living in homeless camps in Tigray and in the capital, Addis Ababa.
sources.headline: How fresh fighting in Tigray could spark wider conflict in Ethiopia

sources.body: Fighting appears to be worsening in Ethiopia after the TPLF said it was in a "full blown" blown war with federal forces this week, days after the Tigrayan rebels declared a coalition with six other armed groups across the country, all with the objective of overthrowing prime minister abiy ahmed's government. And as of friday, it appears that another armed group has claimed to have joined the alliance. More from our correspondent in Addis Ababa Tom Canetti.
sources.headline: Heavy fighting on multiple fronts between Ethiopian forces and rebel groups

stories.headline: Bangkok declares flood disaster after more than 300mm of rain in less than 48 hours

sources.body:
Nonstop rain since Thursday has submerged Thai capital’s roads and canals, sending water into many homes and stores.

Flooding in Bangkok: Disaster zoner declared following heavy rain

Bangkok authorities have declared a disaster zone across all 50 districts of Thailand’s capital after three consecutive days of rainfall caused heavy flooding.

The disaster designation, which gives local organisations authority to take action, came on Saturday after Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said almost 300mm (11.8 inches) of rain had fallen since Thursday afternoon.

The nonstop rain inundated roads and canals with water, sending water into many homes and stores alongside them, according to reports. Photos and videos showed major roads submerged and cars abandoned after drivers were unable to move through the rising water.

Chadchart said the east of the city was most impacted and warned that more rain was forecast again on Saturday. He added that flooding should recede once the rain subsides, as city officials work to drain floodwaters as quickly as possible.

“The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best. We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full,” he said on social media. “The risk areas are those who live near canals. Every canal is now filled.”

Later on Saturday, the government said the flooding situation had “stabilised” but added it would still take two or three days for the water to drain, as long as the rain held off. “If more rainwater doesn’t fall in the area, it will be solved,” he said.

Chadchart also advised residents to move their cars to higher ground, as Bangkok’s public transport authority offered free access to MRT train “park and ride” carparks to store their vehicles until October 2.

Reporting from a flooded street in Bangkok, Al Jazeera’s Tony Cheng said the Thai capital is no stranger to heavy rain during the monsoon season, but the continuous rainfall had locals worried.

“What usually happens is we get heavy downpours for a couple of hours, then you’ll see the street often flooded but it would flow away into the drains quickly, and it would only happen in isolated areas too,” he said.

“What’s happening here is … happening all across the city. This is not a flash flood; this is persistent heavy rain since Thursday evening, and it shows no sign of letting up.”

Somkid Pheuk-ngam, 67, a vendor who lives near a canal just north of central Bangkok, said she had to close her shop for two days.

“The water keeps coming in. It’s hard to go out now. It’s at my waist level,” she told the AFP news agency. “I cannot go anywhere,” she said, adding that this was “worse than the 2011 flood.”

Widespread flooding across Thailand in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.

The Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation has warned of low pressure across eastern, northeastern and central Thailand until Sunday, saying there was a risk of flash floods, forest runoff, mudslides and river overflow.
sources.headline: Disaster zone declared across Bangkok as heavy rain triggers flooding

sources.body: Thailand’s capital Bangkok declared a flood disaster on Saturday after more than 300 millimetres of rain in less than 48 hours, leaving canals overflowing and streets submerged. “It’s like at my waist level now,” a local said. The governor has urged people not to panic, saying the situation is stabilising.
sources.headline: Bangkok declares flood disaster after massive 48-hour downpour

stories.headline: EU releases €6.6 billion to reimburse member states for weapons supplied to Ukraine

sources.body: European Union countries have agreed to release €6.6 billion from a fund meant to reimburse member states that have provided arms to Ukraine, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Friday. At least seven people were killed in Russian strikes on Kyiv earlier in the day, according to local authorities.
sources.headline: EU releases €6.6 billion for members arming Ukraine as seven killed in Kyiv

stories.headline: Supreme Court allows Trump administration to use Social Security data for voter-citizenship checks

sources.body: President Donald Trump wants to let states use a federal database that includes voters’ personal information to check for noncitizens on voter rolls.
sources.headline: Government can use Social Security data to identify noncitizen voters, Supreme Court rules

sources.body: The US Supreme Court on Friday ruled the Trump administration can use a controversial new federal database that would ostensibly verify voter citizenship in November’s elections. Critics argue the administration is exaggerating the threat of non-citizen voters – an extreme rarity in US elections – to implement policies that would disenfranchise likely Democratic voters.
sources.headline: US Supreme Court allows Trump to use controversial voter 'verification' system

stories.headline: Trump plans October campaign swing through deep-red states as Republicans worry about the midterms

sources.body: President Donald Trump is hitting the campaign trail — and a series of his stops are in deep-red states he comfortably won in 2024. Trump will campaign in Iowa, Florida, Texas and Alaska ahead of Election Day, according to two people with knowledge of the matter, who were granted anonymity to discuss not-yet-public plans. That’s on top of his scheduled stop in Oklahoma next week, as the RNC announced , and his visit to Alabama, which POLITICO first reported . While the president has indicated a desire to stump for Ken Paxton in Texas and Dan Sullivan in Alaska, the addition of Iowa and Florida to his campaign schedule signals an expanded focus on red states as Republicans grow increasingly nervous heading into the final stretch of the midterms. The president is also preparing to hold campaign rallies in more traditional battleground states starting Oct. 3, according to one of the people. His travel schedule is a clear signal that the GOP is seeking to shore up their own territory — as rising voter anger over sky-high costs and mass deportations creates new openings for Democrats. The six confirmed states have highly watched Senate, House and gubernatorial contests this November, but they are also ones Trump won by double digits two years ago. “While Democrats squabble over the last two cents their party has to spare, the president is barnstorming the country, energizing our base, and supercharging Republican candidates in key races and beyond,” said Natalie Baldassarre, an RNC spokesperson. “ We have the resources to spend, and Republicans are full steam ahead to protect and expand our majorities,” Baldassarre added. The White House referred POLITICO to the RNC. Vice President JD Vance will also ramp up his campaign travel ahead of Election Day. He and Trump are expected to make stops in Ohio to boost GOP Sen. Jon Husted, as POLITICO has reported . Husted is trailing former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown in internal GOP polling by top Senate Republicans, according to two other people with direct knowledge of the matter, granted anonymity to share private details. Trump’s latest midterms travel swing will first start with Oklahoma and Alabama — two deep-red states where Democrats haven’t made the same inroads in statewide elections as they have in other traditionally conservative states like Texas, Alaska and Kansas. But his Alabama event could help drive turnout and shore up support for GOP state Rep. Rhett Marques, who is in a competitive race with Democratic Rep. Shomari Figures in the state’s 2nd District, despite Republicans’ effort to redraw the seat in their favor. Republicans in Iowa, Texas and Alaska are growing increasingly alarmed about how close their Senate races are amid fallout from the Iran war and other policy moves by Trump. Florida Republicans have become uneasy about their own firewall , with some polling showing statewide races inside the margin of error. Rep. Ashley Hinson, the GOP Senate nominee in Iowa, recently publicly broke with Trump over the Iran war, as did several other Iowa House Republicans. “The bigger question on everything continues to be, whatever you do, will there be enough time. I just don’t know,” said one person close to the White House. “We’re teetering on the edge of it doesn’t matter anymore.” Alec Hernández contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Trump will hit several deep-red states in October campaign blitz

stories.headline: Poll finds a growing divide among Trump voters over the aggressiveness of mass deportations

sources.body: President Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign is running into resistance within his own voter coalition, as more and more Republican candidates publicly break with him ahead of the November election. New results from The POLITICO Poll help explain why: Non-MAGA Trump voters are more than twice as likely as self-identified MAGA Trump voters to say his mass deportation campaign is too aggressive, 31% to 14%. While roughly similar shares of both groups believe Trump’s campaign is about right, the MAGA base wants him to go even further: 36% of MAGA Trump voters say his campaign is not aggressive enough , compared with 23% of non-MAGA Trump voters. Meanwhile, support across Trump’s entire voter coalition falls when it comes to deporting people beyond the most violent offenders, such as those with minor criminal offenses or who have been living in the U.S. for years without legal status. The new survey, conducted by London-based Public First, reveals how Trump’s immigration agenda — which has long been one of his signature political issues and a reliable GOP rallying point — has divided the very coalition that helped power his two presidential wins. The president’s MAGA loyalists are still more inclined than other Trump voters to support a tougher immigration posture, but there are clear limits to how far voters want the administration to go. Those intraparty tensions burst into public view this month, when Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.) released a campaign ad pushing back against Trump’s deportation agenda, saying some of his efforts “have gone too far” and that Hispanic voters who supported him in 2024 “feel betrayed.” It was a remarkable break from a sitting GOP lawmaker over one of the president’s defining policies, as Democrats have locked in on Florida’s 27th District as a prime target in their bid to flip the House. Salazar’s public rift with Trump exemplifies the fears Republicans had been privately warning about for months: that the president’s immigration enforcement — marked last year by high-profile, flashy raids that rippled through communities — was alienating moderate Republicans, independents, young voters and Latinos who support border security and immigration enforcement in theory but dislike how it is being carried out. And as the party stares down a difficult midterm landscape, including in districts and states Trump won in 2024 , other GOP candidates followed Salazar’s lead, increasingly putting distance between themselves and the administration on key issues like immigration — despite having voted last year to approve billions of dollars for border security and immigration enforcement. On Wednesday, Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kan.), whose race has tightened against Democrat Adam Hamilton, also softened his stance on Immigration and Customs Enforcement as raids in southwest Kansas prompt temporary business closures and schools. “When ICE operates in Kansas, it needs to coordinate with our local law enforcement. Our sheriffs and police know these communities better than anyone, and working together keeps officers and residents safe,” he wrote on social media, adding that he’s been in direct contact with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. The POLITICO Poll finds most Americans — including majorities of both MAGA and non-MAGA Trump voters — believe people convicted of serious violent or sexual offenses should be prioritized for deportation, underscoring broad agreement on a more targeted approach to enforcement. The survey also finds that few people — including among both MAGA and non-MAGA Trump voters — prioritized targeting other groups for deportations. Less than a quarter of each group say people convicted of minor criminal offenses should be prioritized. Support falls further when voters are asked about prioritizing people who have lived in the U.S. for several years without legal status or people with dependent children in the U.S. “A lot of it has to do with how you talk about it. They don’t want amnesty for people who have broken the law. They want everybody to do it the right way,” said a person close to the White House granted anonymity to discuss how Republicans are viewing the issue. “They understand that some people might be law-abiding, hard working.” White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said POLITICO is “skewing data to paint a false narrative.” “The American people sent President Trump back to the White House to stop the invasion of our country and deport the millions of illegal aliens Biden and Democrats allowed into the country. The president is delivering on his promises,” she said. Days after releasing the ad, Salazar said she had a “fantastic conversation” with Trump and urged him to protect the political “fortune” he had brought to the Republican Party on immigration. She also told CBS last weekend that Trump and the average American understand “the between the narco and the nanny and the gangster and the gardener.” She said the administration should distinguish between criminals and unauthorized immigrants working in crucial industries such as agriculture, construction, hospitality and health care. That distinction is also reflected in The POLITICO Poll. Both MAGA and non-MAGA Trump voters are open to maintaining or increasing the number of people coming into the U.S. to work in sectors facing labor shortages, such as health care or agriculture. Sixty-five percent of MAGA Trump voters and 69% non-MAGA Trump voters say they want to see about the same number — or more — people coming to the U.S. to work in those sectors facing labor shortages. “Trump 2.0 that took over in January 2025 completely misread what voters were telling him and Joe Biden during 2024, which was that they wanted to see more order and security over the U.S.-Mexico border,” said Matt Barreto, who conducted polling for former Vice President Kamala Harris’ 2024 campaign. “Instead, what Trump told Americans was, ‘Now I’m going to go hunt down immigrants who are just working and contributing to America.’ And there was extremely limited support for that.” Past POLITICO polling on immigration has shown that the Trump administration has been unable to reverse the damage with voters on the issue. Last fall, battleground Republicans were already expressing concern about the administration’s immigration tactics. Those concerns intensified in the months that followed, while negative voter sentiment hardened by April after federal agents killed two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis. The Trump administration, in the wake of bipartisan outrage, softened its rhetoric and abandoned flashy raids that often devolved into clashes with protesters. The president also installed Mullin, who moved quickly to repair relationships on Capitol Hill and keep the Department of Homeland Security out of the headlines. But Mullin is also facing pressure from MAGA critics and immigration hardliners who think he’s not committed to the president’s vow to deport millions of unauthorized immigrants. In an effort to shore up his support with that contingent, top administration accounts, including Mullin’s, have ramped up posts about ICE, arrests statistics and tough talk about the administration’s immigration enforcement agenda.
sources.headline: Poll: A crack is emerging in Trump’s coalition over deportations

stories.headline: Spanish government prepares decree to speed returns of migrants to Morocco
PP and Vox support a Madrid protest over the Ceuta migration crisis

sources.body:
La II Marcha por la Dignidad, convocada por Sociedad Civil Española, ha comenzado poco después de las diez de la mañana desde la madrileña plaza de Cibeles bajo el lema 'Por la dignidad y en defensa de España'. La previsión es que concluya en el Arco del Triunfo, en Moncloa. Entre los asistentes, se encuentra el secretario general del PP, Miguel Tellado, que ha pedido que los migrantes sean devueltos a Marruecos: "Los que han invadido Ceuta deben irse por donde han llegado". Ha insistido en que el Gobierno no hizo nada a pesar, dice, de que estaba alertado de la llegada masiva: "Hay un sentir común de que el Gobierno no ha actuado de forma responsable. Hay una negligencia máxima ya que lo sabía y no actuó. Se cruzó de brazos y dejó que más de 80.000 invasores llegaran".

"España está desprotegida. Ceuta ha sido víctima de una invasión hace dos meses. España no actuó a pesar de que tenían información y después de la invasión tampco está actuando", ha añadido. Tellado ha agradecido "la labor heroica" de las autoridades ceutíes, del PP. "Hay más sentido de Estado en Vivas que en todo el Gobierno", ha asegurado.

También participa el presidente de Vox, Santiago Abascal, que ha insistido en que los migrantes que llegaron deben regresar a su país y ha cargado contra la gestión del Gobierno: "Ceuta sigue invadida porque Sánchez sigue siendo el siervo de Marruecos. Se promueve la invasión migratoria".

El presidente de Vox, Santiago Abascal, atiende a los medios durante la marcha.  Matias Chiofalo Matias Chiofalo / Europa Press

"No creo en nada lo que haga este Gobierno. Ha dicho a los ceutíes que tienen que acostumbrarse a una realidad estructural. La desconfianza es total", ha añadido. Además, ha afirmado que no entiende la actitud el PP al no apoyar la propuesta de su partido para activar el artículo 102 de la Constitución para juzgar a Sánchez por traición.

Alrededor de 8.300 inmigrantes irregulares están alojados en diferentes centros habilitados en Ceuta, aunque se calcula que todavía permanecen en las calles más de 4.000. El Gobierno cifra en 2.048 el número de menores ya identificados y calcula que quedan entre 700 y 1.000.

Marruecos ha acusado a España de obstaculizar la devolución de los inmigrantes que quedan en Ceuta . El pasado jueves, los ministros de Asuntos Exteriores de ambos países, José Manuel Albares y Nasser Bourita, se reunieron en Nueva York para abordar el tema y el representante del Gobierno marroquí se refirió a los "obstáculos" y "polémicas" que, según él, alimenta parte de la clase política española y no permiten zanjar la crisis.

A esta protesta acuden miembros del Partido Popular y de Vox. Este viernes, el vicesecretario general de Hacienda, Vivienda e Infraestructuras del Partido Popular, Juan Bravo, defendió en Ceuta que se agilicen las devoluciones de los migrantes que continúan en la ciudad autónoma a sus países de origen. Bravo asegura que una modificación legislativa podría estar resuelta en una semana para que el Gobierno pudiera ejecutar de inmediato esos retornos.

stories.headline: Government races to negotiate an anti-eviction housing package after the Maricarmen case

sources.body:
Juan Carlos Merino , Asier Martiarena , Fernando H. Valls

“Tenemos que hacer más”, admitió ayer el ministro de la Presidencia, el socialista Félix Bolaños, que reivindicó las políticas de vivienda del Gobierno, pero asumió que “no es suficiente”, ante la enorme indignación social provocada por el desahucio de Maricarmen en Madrid. Y, con una negociación en curso contrarreloj con todos los socios de investidura, confió en que el Consejo de Ministros del próximo martes pueda aprobar “un paquete de medidas potente, completo, para facilitar el acceso a la vivienda a personas que tienen dificultades económicas y para evitar desahucios tan traumáticos, y que tanto nos conmovieron, como el del pasado miércoles de Maricarmen”.

Para conseguirlo, no obstante, Bolaños reclamó “altura de miras y responsabilidad” a la mayoría de la investidura que después tendrá en su mano la convalidación de este decreto ley en el Congreso. “Estamos hablando con todos los grupos parlamentarios que desean llegar a un acuerdo”, admitió el ministro, lo que solo excluye al PP y Vox, a los que situó “al servicio de los especuladores”.

El reto obliga al Ejecutivo a tratar de conciliar a la carrera las discrepantes posiciones de Junts o PNV con las de Podemos. Pero Bolaños destacó que todos los grupos de la investidura tienen “la voluntad” de alcanzar un acuerdo. El drama de Maricarmen no sólo forzó al PSOE a reaccionar, sino que también puede ayudar a superar los vetos cruzados entre las formaciones negociadoras. El objetivo es alumbrar una ley amplia con medidas contundentes que actúen directamente sobre el gran problema de los españoles y que todas ellas superen el trámite de convalidación en el Congreso.

Bolaños evitó más concreción sobre las medidas en discusión, que prefirió mantener “fuera de foco”. “Cuando las negociaciones son públicas, se dificulta mucho llegar a un acuerdo”, se excusó. Pero Junts vuelve a poner sobre la mesa sus propuestas y, esta vez, su portavoz, Miriam Nogueras, admite que en el Ejecutivo las ven “con buenos ojos”. El grupo catalán centra sus reivindicaciones en desgravaciones en el IRPF para inquilinos e hipotecados, así como la prohibición de desahuciar en pisos propiedad de grandes fondos de inversión, lo que evitaría casos como el de Maricarmen. Junts también plantea limitar las compras de grandes fondos.

Otra propuesta que está estudiando el Gobierno recuperar es la congelación de los alquileres que estuvo en vigor durante unas semanas en abril, ya que el decreto acabó decayendo. La medida, si entra en vigor, permitirá que los arrendatarios puedan solicitar una extensión obligatoria del contrato durante un plazo máximo de dos años en las mismas condiciones. Asimismo, Vivienda estudia regular los alquileres temporales a través de una reforma de la ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos (LAU) en la que se incluyan con medidas concretas para que no sirvan de alojamiento inestable a familias o jóvenes.

Los datos son contundentes: en Madrid, la oferta se ha triplicado respecto a 2023, y en ciudades como Barcelona, Cádiz o Donosti los contratos de temporada representan en torno a ocho de cada diez anuncios en los portales inmobiliarios. De la negociación podría caerse la modificación de ley del Suelo para agilitar tramitaciones urbanísticas, ya que es una línea roja para Podemos.
sources.headline: El Gobierno acelera para sellar un pacto antidesahucios

sources.body:
El escándalo social por el caso ha corrido como la pólvora. El desahucio de Maricarmen , la vecina madrileña de 87 años a la que sacaron de su casa, en la que llevaba viviendo más de 70 años, se convertía en el rostro de las miles de situaciones iguales que ocurren cada año.

El injusto sufrimiento de Maricarmen tal vez evite a otros muchos pasar por lo mismo. Y es que, tras la indignación ciudadana, los políticos parecen avergonzados por su inacción. Todos los partidos quieren ahora una solución inmediata al problema de la vivienda . El problema que más preocupa a los españoles, según todas las encuestas. Queda por ver si alcanzarán el acuerdo necesario. Para empezar, en el seno del Gobierno y, después, entre el Ejecutivo y sus socios de investidura.

Mientras se mantienen contactos discretos en esa dirección, algunas de las cosas que se dicen en público dan la impresión de estar ante una subasta, un «quién da más», como la idea de Sumar para que el Gobierno expropie al fondo buitre la casa en la que vivía Maricarmen. Pero, ante tan llamativa propuesta, nos preguntamos, preguntamos a Sumar: ¿para cuántas Maricármenes está dispuesto a aprobar expropiaciones por decreto? ¿O solo esta vez? Tal vez sería mejor reflexionar antes de lanzar titulares.

Pedro Sánchez arrancaba esta legislatura prometiendo conseguir que lo que llamó «el quinto pilar», es decir, la vivienda, dejara de ser un problema en España. No lo ha conseguido hasta ahora y le quedan pocos meses de actividad parlamentaria.

Lo cierto es que lo ha intentado en varias ocasiones con decretos aprobados en Consejo de Ministros que fracasaron por el rechazo del Congreso. Esos reiterados reveses hacían temer lo peor. No es fácil, desde luego, que Podemos y Junts voten lo mismo . Pues esta vez tal vez Maricarmen haya conseguido poner luz al final del túnel. Ponerles la cara colorada a sus señorías.

El problema fue, una y otra vez, que el Ejecutivo no tuvo en el Congreso los escaños de todos sus socios de investidura. Ahora hay esperanza . Y es que, ante el impresionante reproche social, es muy difícil negarse a dar una salida. Así que puede que el Gobierno consiga el apoyo necesario entre la derecha catalana y vasca, por un lado, y los socios de izquierda, por otro.

PP y Vox, como siempre, están fuera de la ecuación . Su no, salvo gran sorpresa, está prácticamente garantizado. Sin embargo, si, como parece en estos momentos, el resto de la Cámara piensa más en los ciudadanos que en sus intereses partidarios, miles de españoles podrán respirar.

Los tribunales volvían a entrar en la escena política esta semana por la apertura de juicio oral a Begoña Gómez y la reactivación del caso Zapatero. Todo, casualmente, por enésima vez, recuerdan los socialistas, coincidiendo con un viaje internacional de Sánchez. Una coincidencia que fuentes de Moncloa consideraban «intolerable».

Las polémicas joyas del expresidente volvían a aparecer en portada después de conocerse su última versión. Se trataría de «un obsequio realizado como atención personal» por el rey de Arabia Saudí, Abdalá bin Abdulaziz al Saud, en un viaje a Madrid en 2007 y durante una reunión en Moncloa.
sources.headline: Los desahucios tienen nombre: Maricarmen

stories.headline: Judge Juan Carlos Peinado, who led the investigation involving Begoña Gómez, is compulsorily retired

sources.body:
El Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) ha publicado este sábado la jubilación forzosa por edad del juez Juan Carlos Peinado, un día antes de cumplir 72 años, y con una carrera marcada en su etapa final por investigar y enviar a juicio ante un jurado popular a Begoña Gómez, esposa del presidente del Gobierno.

La publicación por parte del BOE de la orden del Consejo General del Poder Judicial que declara la jubilación forzosa por edad de Peinado llega un día después de que el juez pasara su último día en el Juzgado de Instrucción 41 de Madrid.

Previamente, durante esta semana ha gozado de tres días de permiso una vez dictó el lunes su última decisión: el auto de apertura de juicio por presunto tráfico de influencias y malversación contra Begoña Gómez y su asesora.

Como tenía previsto, y tras sus vacaciones de verano, ponía así punto y final a una instrucción no exenta de polémica, en la que ha llegado a comparar el caso de Begoña Gómez con conductas "más propias de regímenes absolutistas" y al reinado de Fernando VII.

En estos dos años y medio, en los que pidió permiso para extender su jubilación hasta el máximo legal, Peinado ha pasado por la Moncloa para interrogar al presidente del Gobierno y al ministro de Justicia ―al que incluso pidió imputar sin éxito―, ha llegado a imputar a siete personas, incluido el delegado del Gobierno en Madrid, y ha investigado cinco delitos.

Con decisiones controvertidas como las citaciones en sábado, domingo o Miércoles Santo , Peinado recibió reveses, pero también avales de la Audiencia de Madrid, que finalmente ha ratificado que el juicio a Begoña Gómez sea ante un jurado.

Aunque conocido en el entorno judicial de Madrid, Juan Carlos Peinado era un desconocido para el gran público hasta que la denuncia de Manos Limpias contra Begoña Gómez llegó a sus manos en abril de 2024.

Ese caso ha marcado la recta final de su carrera en la judicatura, a la que llegó tarde, con 40 años, tras haber ejercido como abogado y como secretario del ayuntamiento de varios municipios madrileños.

Se jubila como juez de instrucción del juzgado 41 de Madrid, de Plaza de Castilla, donde lleva la última década. Antes pasó por juzgados de localidades de Ávila, Toledo, Albacete y Madrid, según fuentes jurídicas consultadas por EFE.

Desde el 41 ha llevado otros casos también conocidos en su momento como el del triple crimen en un despacho de abogados del barrio madrileño de Usera en 2016 ―que acabó juzgado en Venezuela―, o una demanda, ya archivada, contra los concejales Pablo Soto y Guillermo Zapata por mensajes ofensivos en redes sociales en 2015.

Abrió incluso diligencias contra el exfutbolista Raúl González Blanco por presunta ocultación de patrimonio y fue sonada la imputación, en 2019, de periodistas por presunta revelación de secretos vinculada al sumario de los Comités de Defensa de la República (CDR), ya archivada.

Una causa contra un cargo de la empresa municipal de transportes de Madrid (EMT) acabó archivada tras agotarse el plazo de instrucción, y también ha investigado el supuesto hackeo de los correos de la pareja de la presidenta madrileña, Isabel Díaz Ayuso , o una denuncia de Hazte Oír contra el alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida , por la paralización de un autobús reivindicativo.
sources.headline: El BOE publica la jubilaci�n forzosa por edad del juez Peinado

sources.body:
El juez Juan Carlos Peinado en los alrededores de los juzgados de Plaza Castilla. / José Luis Roca

El viernes 25 de septiembre fue el último día del juez Juan Carlos Peinado en la plaza número 41 de Instrucción del Tribunal de Instancia de Madrid. Este sábado, el Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) ha publicado su jubilación forzosa. Y este domingo cumple 72 años, que es la edad máxima a la que se puede llegar siendo juez --tras haber solicitado una prórroga para seguir en servicio activo hace dos años--, y abandona su puesto tras haber concluido la instrucción del 'caso Begoña' y haber mandado ante un jurado popular a la esposa de Pedro Sánchez y a su asistente en Moncloa. Su investigación ha sido varias veces corregida (más bien pulida y reconducida) por la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid y muy cuestionada tanto en ámbitos jurídicos como políticos.

Peinado era un juez más de los de instrucción con despacho en la Plaza de Castilla de la capital hasta que, en abril de 2024 saltó a primera línea mediática tras abrir causa contra Begoña Gómez. Actuaba a raíz de una denuncia de Manos Limpias -- a la que más tarde se unieron Hazte Oír, Vox o Iustitia Europa, entre otros--por una supuesta influencia de la esposa del Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez en asuntos como el rescate de Air Europa y sus relaciones con Globalia, pero esa primera acusación fue ampliándose a otros aspectos de la actividad profesional de la esposa de Sánchez, en especial sus colaboraciones universitarias, y Gómez ha acabado procesada por delitos de tráfico de influencias y malversación de fondos públicos.

Boletín Oficial del Estado donde se declara la jubilación forzosa del juez Peinado. / EL PERIÓDICO

La última semana de Peinado en su juzgado ha sido especial, únicamente ha trabajado el lunes y el viernes -- el resto ha disfrutado de días de vacaciones que le quedaban pendientes--, pero comenzó con la notificación de una de las decisiones más importantes de su carrera, la apertura de juicio contra Gómez y su asistente Cristina Álvarez.

Lo argumenta por el "salto cualitativo" que dio su carrera profesional desde la llegada de Pedro Sánchez al poder y el uso propio de su asesora, pagada con los Presupuestos Generales del Estado, en relación con una cátedra que codirigió en la Universidad Complutense titulado Transformación Social Competitiva y la financiación y uso de un software asociado al curso.

La instrucción de Peinado sobre este asunto ha sufrido continuas correcciones por parte de la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid a resultas de los recursos que han interpuesto contra casi la práctica totalidad de sus decisiones tanto las defensas como la Fiscalía, que desde el inicio no ha visto razones para proceder penalmente contra la esposa del presidente del Gobierno.

Además, algunas de sus resoluciones han destacado por lo excéntrico de sus argumentos , como la que el pasado mes de abril afirmaba la falta de antecedentes en democracia de conductas que "provienen de palacios presidenciales, como este supuesto, parecen más propias de regímenes absolutistas, por suerte, ya olvidados en el tiempo en nuestro Estado, lo que obliga a tratar de analizar ( quizás hubiera que remontarse al reinado de Fernando VII) ".
sources.headline: Adiós a Peinado: el juez del caso Begoña se jubila tras una instrucción cuestionada por la calle y reconducida desde la Audiencia Provincial

stories.headline: Renfe says cyberattack through compromised Adif servers exposed limited user data

sources.body:
Renfe denuncia un hackeig amb robatori de dades d'usuaris a través de servidors informàtics d'Adif.

Segons ha confirmat el Ministeri de Transports i Mobilitat Sostenible, "Renfe ha estat objecte d'un incident de ciberseguretat " a servidors d'Adif "prèviament compromesos". L'operador ferroviari descarta que l'atac hagi afectat la circulació de trens.

Des d'aquest matí s'havien detectat incidències a les pàgines web de Renfe i Adif. Segons han comentat alguns usuaris a les xarxes, hi apareixia un missatge que informava que el lloc web no estava operatiu i, durant una estona, hi apareixia la figura d'un gat negre.

El web d'adif ha mostrat durant algunes hores la foto d'un gat en comptes del contingut original. No és una broma d'Internet: he parlat amb premsa d'ADIF, em confirmen atac. Em diuen que no ha afectat operacions ferroviàries ni dades. Està a la wayback machine. pic.twitter.com/Ehx71YOQL4

Al vespre, en entrar a la pàgina d'Adif, el que es pot veure és això:

El ministeri ha activat els protocols de resposta i ha desplegat " mesures extraordinàries de protecció " amb el suport d'especialistes independents en ciberseguretat.

Els atacants han tingut accés a informació privada dels usuaris de Renfe –noms i adreces de correu electrònic– però, segons fonts ministerials, no hi ha evidències que hagin pogut accedir a dades bancàries, números de DNI, mitjans de pagament o altres informacions "sensibles".

Segons Renfe, l'incident es produeix després de "diverses setmanes" d'intents "continuats" d'accedir als seus sistemes informàtics.

Dijous a última hora la companyia va detectar una activitat inusual en els sistemes que van aconseguir contenir amb les eines de ciberseguretat de què disposen.
sources.headline: Un ciberatac a Renfe i Adif aconsegueix accedir a "informació limitada" dels usuaris

sources.body: (ACN) Renfe ha denunciat un robatori de dades d’usuaris a través de servidors informàtics d’ Adif . Segons la companyia, els ciberdelinqüents poden haver accedit a informació “limitada”, principalment noms i adreces de correu electrònic , tot i que admet que l’anàlisi “continua en curs”. Amb la informació que disposa actualment, no s’han identificat evidències “concloents” sobre si aquesta informació ha estat difosa públicament. L’empresa ferroviària subratlla que no hi ha constància d’accés a dades bancàries, financeres, mitjans de pagament, DNI o altres informacions “especialment sensibles”. Segons Renfe, l’incident es produeix després de “diverses setmanes” d’intents “continuats” d’accedir als seus sistemes informàtics. També et pot interessar Un ciberatac deixa al descobert dades d’inscrits a la Borsa d’Habitatges de Lloguer de Barcelona Maria Solans 2 minuts de lectura Servidors informàtics Fonts de Renfe han explicat que l’origen de l’incident se situa “en servidors d’Adif prèviament compromesos que mantenien interconnexió amb els sistemes de la companyia”. També han indicat que, un cop s’ha detectat el ciberatac, s’han activat els protocols de resposta , s’han “aïllat els entorns afectats” i s’han desplegat mesures “extraordinàries de protecció”. Adif denuncia ciberatacs La gestora pública de les infraestructures ferroviàries ha denunciat l’atac i ha posat tota la informació que ha recollit a disposició del Centre Criptològic Nacional (CNN). Alhora, les dades s’han traslladat a les empreses proveïdores “amb possibilitat de veure’s afectades” perquè puguin prendre les mesures oportunes. Finalment, Adif assegura que cap aplicació ni sistema relacionat amb l’explotació ferroviària ha resultat afectat. La circulació ferroviària “està garantida i es desenvolupa en condicions de normalitat”.
sources.headline: Renfe denuncia un robatori de dades d’usuaris a través de servidors informàtics d’Adif

stories.headline: Barcelona TMB bus workers announce seven days of partial strikes in October

sources.body:
La plantilla dels autobusos de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) ha anunciat set dies més d'aturades parcials durant el mes d'octubre, després que aquesta setmana no s'hagi assolit un preacord amb l'empresa que permetés desconvocar la vaga.

L'assemblea de treballadors ha decidit convocar protestes per als dies 8, 14, 15, 20, 22, 27 i 29 d'octubre en tres franges de dues hores: de nou a onze del matí, de set de la tarda a nou de la nit i d'onze de la nit a una de la matinada.

La plataforma sindical unitària va presentar dilluns una proposta que la direcció va assumir "pràcticament en la seva totalitat" , segons ha explicat la UGT en un comunicat.

En l'assemblea de dilluns, la plantilla va donar quinze dies a l'empresa per tancar una "proposta satisfactòria" per al nou conveni. Els treballadors van anunciar que hi hauria més aturades parcials si no s'arribava a un acord durant aquest termini.

Aquesta proposta, però, només havia de servir per desconvocar les aturades , no per tancar la negociació pel conveni col·lectiu, que continua oberta.

La proposta preveia una millora progressiva dels calendaris laborals , l'aplicació esglaonada de la jornada de 35 hores –amb tretze dies de descans generats fins al 2029– i l'entrada de 200 persones a la plantilla estructural, a més d'increments salarials i una prima única d'uns 650 euros si el conveni es tancava abans d'acabar l'any.

Segons la UGT, "a última hora" un dels sindicats va considerar que la proposta "no era prou bona" i va plantejar "continuar" negociant per aconseguir més millores. La resta de forces van acceptar la proposta "sempre amb la premissa de mantenir la unitat sindical", amb el compromís que fos l'assemblea qui prengués la decisió final.

Davant aquest escenari, l'empresa "va decidir trencar la negociació" i la Generalitat, que feia de mediador, "va entendre que, en aquestes condicions, no es podia assolir un acord, atès que l'empresa manifestava que no podia oferir més".

En aquest escenari, l'assemblea de treballadors ha decidit mantenir les aturades i seguir pressionant l'empresa per aconseguir millores.
sources.headline: La plantilla d'autobusos de TMB anuncia set dies de vagues parcials a l'octubre

stories.headline: Catalonia’s internal reservoirs begin autumn more than 75% full

sources.body: Els embassaments de les conques internes de Catalunya han començat la tardor encara amb unes reserves hídriques que superen el 75 % de la seva capacitat màxima . Es tracta d’una dada que millora lleugerament la de l’any passat i que dista molt de la sequera que encara arrossegàvem fa només dos anys. També et pot interessar Estat dels embassaments a Catalunya 2026, a temps real: nivell dels pantans | GRÀFICS Clara Aliaguilla Marcos Amores Sánchez 1 minut de lectura Veníem de gairebé un ple tècnic El cert és que vam arribar a l’inici de l’estiu amb els embassaments gairebé plens a vessar . Aleshores, les conques internes de Catalunya acumulaven 633 hm³ d’aigua que representaven més del 90 % de la seva capacitat. Aquest ple tècnic ha permès afrontar l’estiu més calorós registrat mai amb plenes garanties pel que fa a la disponibilitat d’aigua. La gran evaporació i la manca de grans tempestes durant bona part de l’estiu han comportat, juntament amb la gran demanda d’aigua d’aquestes dates, una pèrdua de 123 hm³ d’aigua en els darrers tres mesos. Es tracta d’un descens marcat, però no pas excepcional i, a més a més, parteix de la base que veníem de molt amunt. Sense anar gaire lluny, els estius del 2019 i 2021 la pèrdua del recurs hídric durant l’estiu va ser encara superior , de 162 i 131 hm³, respectivament, aleshores també amb un punt de partida molt alt a finals de juny. També et pot interessar L’agost del 2026, entre els més càlids de l’últim segle a Barcelona, tanca l’estiu més calorós mai registrat Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo 4 minuts de lectura Gairebé 100 hm³ per sobre de la mitjana Els gairebé 510 hm³ d’aigua emmagatzemats aquests dies suposen una mica més del 75 % de la seva capacitat màxima i gairebé 100 hm³ per sobre de la mitjana del segle XXI, que se situa en 423 hm³, 87 menys que en l’actualitat. Això permet continuar afrontant amb garanties la resta de l’any , més tenint en compte que ara arriba un dels teòrics òptims pluviomètrics de l’any, la tardor, que acostuma a coincidir amb una aturada en el descens de les reserves hídriques. Panoràmica del pantà, sortida sol, fumejant lleugerament. SAU @ElTiempo_tve @jjanue @mauri_francesc @daniramirez @SoniaPapell @TomasMolinaB @jacobpetrus_tve @3CatInfoelTemps @SergiLoras @gemmapuigf @jaure_10 @lasextameteo @3CatInfoelTemps @AEMET_Cat pic.twitter.com/NHj60VxBed — CARME MOLIST VIDAL (@carmemolist) September 24, 2026 El sistema Ter-Llobregat, que abasteix l’àrea metropolitana de Barcelona, disposa actualment de gairebé 460 hm³ d’aigua, una mica més del 77 % de la seva capacitat. Les dades, per tant, són òptimes, més si les comparem amb la sequera desastrosa que fa només dos anys justos encara feia trontollar el sistema hídric de Catalunya. La tardor del 2024 va començar amb els embassaments encara per sota del 30 % , però la tardor del 2024 i, molt especialment la primavera del 2025, van aconseguir girar la truita. Que les bones dades actuals no ens facin oblidar d’on venim. També et pot interessar Temps de la tardor del 2026 a Barcelona: ens portarà la fresca? Què en sabem? Manel Cascante Torrella 3 minuts de lectura

stories.headline: Barcelona’s annual saving between the cheapest and most expensive supermarkets reaches €1,823, consumer group says

sources.body: L’estudi anual de supermercats de l’Organització de Consumidor i Usuaris (OCU) analitza el cost del cistell de consum a tot l’estat espanyol. Segons l’anàlisi del 2026 , els preus han tornat a pujar una mitjana d’1,8 %, tot i que es tracta de l’increment més baix en els darrers cinc anys. Així mateix, a diferència del 2025, hi ha vuit cadenes que han abaixat els preus . Segons l’OCU, l’estalvi anual mitjà a Barcelona ciutat entre comprar en un supermercat més barat i en el més car arriba als 1.823 € . També et pot interessar El setembre arriba més costerut que l’any passat: quins productes s’encareixen més? Cristina Brotons Ester Magdaleno Helena Molist Sancho 2 minuts de lectura Cadenes que apugen i abaixen preus Aquest 2026, l’estudi ha recollit 101.520 preus de 609 establiments en 183 ciutats. L’OCU ha elaborat un cistell de consum amb 244 productes amb aliments frescos, alimentació envasada, begudes, productes de neteja, drogueria i higiene. Segons detalla l’estudi, les cadenes d’àmbit estatal que han abaixat els preus són : Carrefour Market , un 2,7 % Lidl , un 1,9 % Mercadona , un 1,8 % Aldi , un 1,4 % E. Leclerc , un 1,3 % Supeco , un 0,6 % Consum , un 0,3 % Familia , un 0,3 % A l’altre cantó de la balança, els supermercats que han apujat preus són: Supercor , un 2,7 % Carrefour Express , un 2,5 % Alcampo , un 2,5 % Hipercor , un 2,3 % El Corte Inglés , amb un 1,5 % Dia , un 1,2 % Caprabo , un 0,8 % En termes generals, l’estudi conclou que les cadenes més barates són Supermercados Dani, Alcampo, Tifer i Family Cash. Mentre que les més cares són Hipercor, Sánchez Romero, Supercor i El Corte Inglés. També et pot interessar L’IPC puja 5 dècimes a l’agost a Catalunya, fins al 4 %, l’encariment més alt des del març del 2023 Redacció 3 minuts de lectura Un encariment de l’1,8 % de mitjana Segons l’estudi, el cistell de consum, que és una mostra representativa de productes bàsics, s’ha encarit un 1,8 % de mitjana . Els que més han pujat de preu són els productes frescos —un 4,7 % de mitjana— impulsats sobretot pel peix, amb un increment de més d’un 8 %. La carn ho ha fet un 3,7 % i les fruites i les verdures un 3,4 %. Els productes envasats, en canvi, s’han apujat un 1,4 %. Els cinc aliments que més s’han apujat : el tomàquet , un 33,2 % les llimones , un 25,2 % la coliflor , un 22,8 % l’albergínia , un 20,4 % la bruixa , un 19,4 % Els productes que més s’han abaixat : el puré de patates , un 14,8 % les carxofes , un 15,1 % els plàtans de Canàries , un 22,6 % els tovallons de paper , un 30,4 % Segons l’OCU, l’estudi demostra que molts preus no han baixat, malgrat que les pujades s’han alentit en aquest darrer any. Assenyala que molts preus es mantenen “excepcionalment alts” , quan una bona part de les famílies no ha recuperat el poder adquisitiu. Per això, l’OCU insisteix que cal reduir l’IVA dels productes bàsics i donar més ajudes per comprar aliments a famílies en situació de vulnerabilitat. sources.headline: Quins supermercats han apujat més els preus aquest 2026, segons l’OCU?

sources.body:
Una mujer repasa la lista de la compra mientras llena el carro en un supermercado de Barcelona. / FERRAN NADEU - EPC

El supermercado en el que se hace la compra puede marcar una diferencia importante en el presupuesto de un hogar. Y en Catalunya, más. Barcelona es la capital de provincia con el nivel de precios más elevado de España , según el último estudio de la Organización de Consumidores y Usuarios (OCU), que sitúa a la ciudad con un índice de 110 frente al 100 que corresponde a la localidad más barata del análisis.

La diferencia no es menor para una familia que compra durante todo el año. Un hogar de Barcelona puede llegar a ahorrar unos 1.823 euros anuales si cambia el establecimiento más caro por el más barato , de acuerdo con los cálculos de OCU. Se trata de la diferencia entre los dos extremos de la oferta comercial de la ciudad para la cesta de productos analizada, no de un ahorro que pueda obtener cualquier consumidor independientemente del supermercado que utilice.

Barcelona no es un caso aislado dentro de Catalunya. La comunidad se encuentra entre las regiones con un mayor nivel de precios de supermercados en el estudio de OCU, junto a Castilla-La Mancha, Castilla y León, País Vasco, La Rioja, Navarra y Cantabria.

Además de Barcelona, varias localidades catalanas aparecen entre las que presentan los índices más elevados. Cerdanyola del Vallès figura entre las ciudades más caras del conjunto del estudio , junto a Getxo (País Vasco), Pozuelo de Alarcón (Comunidad de Madrid) y Majadahonda (Comunidad de Madrid). También aparecen otras localidades del entorno de Barcelona entre las zonas con niveles elevados de precios.

El contraste con otras partes de España es notable. Torrent, Villarreal y Santa Pola , todas en la Comunitat Valenciana, son las localidades con los índices medios más bajos. Junto con Murcia encabezan precisamente el grupo de comunidades con los precios más reducidos.

El estudio también permite comparar las cadenas, aunque el supermercado más barato depende de las enseñas que estén disponibles en cada ciudad . A escala nacional, OCU sitúa a Dani como la cadena con el índice de precios más bajo, seguida de Family Cash y Tifer y, después, Alcampo y Supeco .

Entre las grandes cadenas que operan en buena parte de España, Lidl, Mercadona y Aldi han reducido sus precios respecto al estudio anterior. Lidl destaca especialmente por haber pasado de ser la opción más barata en 18 localidades en 2025 a serlo en 60 localidades en 2026 . Mercadona también duplica el número de ciudades en las que ofrece la cesta más económica, mientras que Supeco pasa de 18 a 28.

En el otro extremo, Sánchez Romero vuelve a registrar el índice más elevado entre las cadenas analizadas, con 176. También aparecen entre las cadenas con mayores niveles de precios Hipercor, El Corte Inglés y Supercor .

La fotografía es diferente cuando se analiza una cesta concreta. OCU señala, por ejemplo, que Carrefour Market ha reducido un 2,7% sus precios , mientras que Lidl los ha bajado un 1,9%, Mercadona un 1,8% y Aldi un 1,4%. En los productos económicos, Mercadona recorta un 5,6% y Lidl un 4,7%.
sources.headline: Barcelona tiene uno de los supermercados más caros de España: esto es lo que puede ahorrar un hogar al año
